title: BS — standard (find exact target)
description: Given an array of integers nums which is sorted in ascending order, and an integer target, write a function to search target in nums. If target exists, then return its index. Otherwise, return -1.

title: BS — leftmost occurrence
description: Given an array of integers nums sorted in non-decreasing order, find the starting position of a given target value. If target is not found in the array, return -1.

title: BS — rightmost occurrence
description: Given an array of integers nums sorted in non-decreasing order, find the ending position of a given target value. If target is not found in the array, return -1.

title: BS — rotated sorted array
description: There is an integer array nums sorted in ascending order (with distinct values) that is rotated at an unknown pivot index. Given the array nums after the possible rotation and an integer target, return the index of target if it is in nums, or -1 if it is not in nums.

title: BS — on answer space (min/max feasibility)
description: A conveyor belt has packages that must be shipped from one port to another within days days. The i-th package on the conveyor belt has a weight of weights[i]. Return the least weight capacity of the ship that will result in all the packages on the conveyor belt being shipped within days days.

title: BFS — standard graph (adjacency list)
description: Given a directed graph represented as an adjacency list graph where graph[i] is a list of nodes that node i points to, and a start node, return a list of nodes in the order they are visited using Breadth-First Search (BFS). Visit neighbors in the order they appear in the list.

title: BFS — level order tree traversal
inputs_given:
root = TreeNode(3)
root.left = TreeNode(9)
root.right = TreeNode(20)
root.right.left = TreeNode(15)
root.right.right = TreeNode(7)
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the level order traversal of its nodes' values. (i.e., from left to right, level by level).

title: Multi-source BFS (grid)
description: You are given an m x n grid where each cell can have one of three values: 0 (empty), 1 (fresh orange), or 2 (rotten orange). Every minute, any fresh orange that is 4-directionally adjacent to a rotten orange becomes rotten. Return the minimum number of minutes that must elapse until no cell has a fresh orange. If this is impossible, return -1.

title: DFS — iterative (explicit stack)
description: Given a directed graph represented as an adjacency list graph where graph[i] is a list of nodes that node i points to, and a start node, return a list of nodes in the order they are visited using an iterative Depth-First Search (DFS) with a stack. Push neighbors in the order they appear, which means the last neighbor is popped and visited first.

title: DFS — recursive (graph, track visited)
description: Given a directed graph represented as an adjacency list graph and a start node, return a list of nodes in the order they are visited using recursive Depth-First Search (DFS). Visit neighbors in the order they appear in the list.

title: Connected components (undirected)
description: You have a graph of n nodes. You are given an integer n and an array edges where edges[i] = [a, b] indicates that there is an undirected edge between a and b in the graph. Return the number of connected components in the graph.

title: Cycle detection — directed graph (DFS 3-color)
description: Given n nodes labeled from 0 to n-1 and a list of directed edges where edges[i] = [u, v] represents a directed edge from node u to node v, return True if the graph contains a cycle, and False otherwise.

title: Bipartite check (BFS 2-coloring)
description: There is an undirected graph with n nodes, where each node is numbered between 0 and n - 1. You are given a 2D array graph, where graph[u] is an array of nodes that node u is adjacent to. Return True if and only if it is bipartite.

title: BFS on grid — 4-directional flood fill
description: An image is represented by an m x n integer grid image where image[i][j] represents the pixel value of the image. You are also given three integers sr, sc, and color. You should perform a flood fill on the image starting from the pixel image[sr][sc] and replacing its color and all connected adjacent pixels of the same color with color.

title: Topo sort — Kahn's algorithm (BFS + in-degree)
description: Given n nodes and a list of directed edges where edges[i] = [u, v] indicates a directed edge from u to v, return a valid topological sort array of the nodes. If no such sort is possible (a cycle exists), behavior is undefined (or return an incomplete list).

title: Topo sort — DFS postorder
description: Given n nodes and a list of directed edges where edges[i] = [u, v] indicates a directed edge from u to v, return a valid topological sort array using DFS postorder reversal. Assume the graph is a DAG.

title: Dijkstra's (min-heap, single source)
description: Given n nodes and a list of directed weighted edges where edges[i] = [u, v, weight], find the shortest path from the src node to all other nodes. Return an array of size n where the value at index i is the shortest distance to node i. If a node is unreachable, the value should be -1.

title: Bellman-Ford (handles negative weights)
description: Given n nodes and a list of directed weighted edges where edges[i] = [u, v, weight] (weights can be negative), find the shortest path from the src node to all other nodes. Return an array of size n where the value at index i is the shortest distance to node i. If a node is unreachable, the value should be -1.

title: Floyd-Warshall (all-pairs shortest path)
description: Given n nodes and a list of directed weighted edges where edges[i] = [u, v, weight], find the shortest path between all pairs of nodes. Return an n x n matrix where matrix[i][j] is the shortest distance from i to j.

title: Prim's MST (min-heap, adjacency list)
description: Given n nodes and a list of undirected weighted edges where edges[i] = [u, v, weight], return the total weight of the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST).

title: Kruskal's MST (sort edges + union-find)
description: Given n nodes and a list of undirected weighted edges where edges[i] = [u, v, weight], return the total weight of the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST).

title: Union-Find — path compression + union by rank
description: Implement a UnionFind class with path compression and union by rank. Then, use it to solve the connected components problem: given n nodes and undirected edges (where edges[i] = [u, v]), return the number of connected components.

title: Tarjan's bridges (critical connections)
description: There are n servers numbered from 0 to n - 1 connected by undirected server-to-server connections forming a network where connections[i] = [a, b]. Return a list of all critical connections (bridges) in the network.

title: Preorder traversal — iterative (root, left, right)
inputs_given:
root = TreeNode(1)
root.right = TreeNode(2)
root.right.left = TreeNode(3)
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the preorder traversal of its nodes' values iteratively.

title: Inorder traversal — iterative (left, root, right)
inputs_given:
root = TreeNode(1)
root.right = TreeNode(2)
root.right.left = TreeNode(3)
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the inorder traversal of its nodes' values iteratively.

title: Postorder traversal — iterative (left, right, root)
inputs_given:
root = TreeNode(1)
root.right = TreeNode(2)
root.right.left = TreeNode(3)
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the postorder traversal of its nodes' values iteratively.

title: LCA — binary tree (DFS recursive)
description: Given a binary tree, find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) of two given nodes p and q in the tree.

title: Validate BST (DFS with min/max bounds)
inputs_given:
root = TreeNode(2)
root.left = TreeNode(1)
root.right = TreeNode(3)
description: Given the root of a binary tree, determine if it is a valid binary search tree (BST).

title: Diameter of binary tree (DFS postorder)
inputs_given:
root = TreeNode(1)
root.left = TreeNode(2)
root.right = TreeNode(3)
root.left.left = TreeNode(4)
root.left.right = TreeNode(5)
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the length of the diameter of the tree. The diameter is the length of the longest path between any two nodes.

title: Max path sum in binary tree (tree DP)
inputs_given:
root = TreeNode(-10)
root.left = TreeNode(9)
root.right = TreeNode(20)
root.right.left = TreeNode(15)
root.right.right = TreeNode(7)
description: A path in a binary tree is a sequence of nodes where each pair of adjacent nodes in the sequence has an edge connecting them. Return the maximum path sum of any non-empty path.

title: Serialize / deserialize binary tree
inputs_given:
root = TreeNode(1)
root.left = TreeNode(2)
root.right = TreeNode(3)
root.right.left = TreeNode(4)
root.right.right = TreeNode(5)
description: Design an algorithm to serialize and deserialize a binary tree. The serialize method converts a tree to a string, and deserialize converts the string back to a tree.

title: Stack — bracket matching (valid parentheses)
description: Given a string s containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid.

title: Stack — evaluate reverse polish notation
description: Evaluate the value of an arithmetic expression in Reverse Polish Notation. Valid operators are +, -, *, /.

title: Monotonic stack — next greater element
description: Given an array nums, find the next greater element for each element in the array. Return an array of the same size. If no greater element exists, output -1.

title: Monotonic deque — sliding window maximum
description: You are given an array of integers nums, there is a sliding window of size k which is moving from the very left of the array to the very right. Return the max sliding window.

title: Merge intervals (sort + greedy)
description: Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [start, end], merge all overlapping intervals.

title: Insert interval (merge with new interval)
description: You are given an array of non-overlapping intervals sorted by their start time, and a new interval. Insert the new interval into the array (merge if necessary).

title: Greedy interval scheduling (minimum arrows)
description: There are some spherical balloons taped onto a flat wall. You are given a 2D integer array points where points[i] = [start, end]. Return the minimum number of arrows that must be shot to burst all balloons.

title: Kth largest element (min-heap of size k)
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k-th largest element in the array.

title: Top K frequent elements (heap + hash map)
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements.

title: Fixed window — max sum subarray of size k
description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, find the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray of size k.

title: Variable window — longest substring without repeating
description: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.

title: Two pointers — pair sum in sorted array
description: Given a 1-indexed array of integers nums that is already sorted in non-decreasing order, find two numbers such that they add up to a specific target number. Return their 0-indexed positions.

title: Dutch National Flag (3-way partition)
description: Given an array nums with n objects colored red, white, or blue, sort them in-place so that objects of the same color are adjacent, with the colors in the order red (0), white (1), and blue (2).

title: Fast/slow pointers — find duplicate (Floyd's on array)
description: Given an array of integers nums containing n + 1 integers where each integer is in the range [1, n] inclusive. There is only one repeated number in nums, return this repeated number. You must solve the problem without modifying the array.

title: Prefix sum — 1D range query
description: Given an integer array nums, handle multiple queries to calculate the sum of the elements of nums between indices left and right inclusive.

title: Kadane's algorithm (max subarray sum)
description: Given an integer array nums, find the contiguous subarray (containing at least one number) which has the largest sum and return its sum.

title: 1D DP — climbing stairs / Fibonacci
description: You are climbing a staircase. It takes n steps to reach the top. Each time you can either climb 1 or 2 steps. In how many distinct ways can you climb to the top?

title: 1D DP — house robber (max non-adjacent)
description: You are a professional robber planning to rob houses along a street. Each house has a certain amount of money stashed, but adjacent houses have security systems connected. Given an integer array nums representing the money of each house, return the maximum amount of money you can rob tonight without alerting the police.

title: 1D DP — coin change (unbounded knapsack)
description: You are given an integer array coins representing coins of different denominations and an integer amount representing a total amount of money. Return the fewest number of coins that you need to make up that amount. If it cannot be made up, return -1.

title: 1D DP — LIS O(n log n) with binary search
description: Given an integer array nums, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

title: 2D DP — LCS (longest common subsequence)
description: Given two strings text1 and text2, return the length of their longest common subsequence. If there is no common subsequence, return 0.

title: 2D DP — edit distance (Levenshtein)
description: Given two strings word1 and word2, return the minimum number of operations required to convert word1 to word2. Operations are insert, delete, or replace a character.

title: 2D DP — unique paths (grid)
description: There is a robot on an m x n grid. The robot is initially located at the top-left corner and tries to move to the bottom-right corner. The robot can only move either down or right at any point in time. Given m and n, return the number of possible unique paths.

title: 2D DP — minimum path sum (grid)
description: Given a m x n grid filled with non-negative numbers, find a path from top left to bottom right, which minimizes the sum of all numbers along its path. You can only move down or right.

title: 0/1 Knapsack — partition equal subset sum
description: Given an integer array nums, return True if you can partition the array into two subsets such that the sum of the elements in both subsets is equal.

title: Interval DP — burst balloons
description: You are given n balloons, indexed from 0 to n - 1. Each balloon is painted with a number on it represented by an array nums. If you burst the i-th balloon, you will get nums[i - 1] * nums[i] * nums[i + 1] coins. Return the maximum coins you can collect by bursting the balloons wisely.

title: DP + memoization — word break
description: Given a string s and a dictionary of strings word_dict, return True if s can be segmented into a space-separated sequence of one or more dictionary words.

title: Bitmask DP — minimum XOR sum / assignment
description: You are given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of length n. The XOR sum of the two arrays is (nums1[0] XOR nums2[0]) + (nums1[1] XOR nums2[1]) + ... + (nums1[n - 1] XOR nums2[n - 1]). Return the minimum XOR sum after rearranging the elements of nums2.

title: Trie — build from scratch (insert / search / startsWith)
inputs_given: ops: insert("apple"), search("apple"), search("app"), startsWith("app"), insert("app"), search("app")
description: A trie (pronounced as 'try') or prefix tree is a tree data structure used to efficiently store and retrieve keys in a dataset of strings. Implement the Trie class with insert, search, and starts_with methods.

title: Backtracking — subsets (power set)
description: Given an integer array nums of unique elements, return all possible subsets (the power set). The solution set must not contain duplicate subsets.

title: Backtracking — permutations
description: Given an array nums of distinct integers, return all the possible permutations. You can return the answer in any order.

title: Backtracking — combination sum (target)
description: Given an array of distinct integers candidates and a target integer target, return a list of all unique combinations of candidates where the chosen numbers sum to target. You may choose the same number from candidates an unlimited number of times.

title: Backtracking — N-Queens
description: The n-queens puzzle is the problem of placing n queens on an n x n chessboard such that no two queens attack each other. Return all distinct solutions. Each solution contains a distinct board configuration of the n-queens' placement, where 'Q' and '.' both indicate a queen and an empty space respectively.

title: KMP — pattern matching (find first occurrence)
description: Given two strings needle and haystack, return the index of the first occurrence of needle in haystack, or -1 if needle is not part of haystack. Implement using KMP or similar efficient algorithm.

title: Sieve of Eratosthenes (count primes < n)
description: Given an integer n, return the number of prime numbers that are strictly less than n.
